top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Tour de Brisbane. Practice on urban road course on fully closed city streets: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 68 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour de Brisbane's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
68 miles on urban road course on fully closed city streets burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
When someone attacks on urban road course on fully closed city streets, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
60ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Tour de Brisbane. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on urban road course on fully closed city streets can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Base fitness for Tour de Brisbane. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
At Tour de Brisbane, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour de Brisbane. Train it until it feels boring.
The aerobic base that lets you ride urban road course on fully closed city streets at tempo for 68 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 4,068ft of climbing on urban road course on fully closed city streets does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.heat: April in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Tour de Brisbane. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for Tour de Brisbane's 68 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Tour de Brisbane rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on urban road course on fully closed city streets with one significant climb to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 68 miles of urban road course on fully closed city streets with one significant climb in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia.
